thread.title: Asian Shares Rise Following Wall Street Gains After Trump's Greenland Reversal
thread.title_full: Asian Shares Rise Following Wall Street Gains After Trump's Greenland Reversal

author: Associated Press Television News
title: Asian Shares Rise Following Wall Street Gains After Trump's Greenland Reversal
text:
• Asian shares mostly advanced on Thursday, tracking Wall Street gains.
• U.S. President Donald Trump walked back from imposing tariffs on eight European countries over Greenland.
• Trump ruled out using military force to take control of Greenland.
• The future for the S&P 500 was up 0.4% on Thursday.
• The Dow Jones Industrial Average increased 0.3%.
• Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 climbed 1.9% to 53,760.85.
• South Korea’s Kospi was up 2% to 5,008.08.
• Hong Kong’s Hang Seng fell 0.2% to 26,531.29.
• The Shanghai Composite index dropped nearly 0.2%, to 4,110.86.
• In Australia, the S&P/ASX 200 traded 0.7% higher to 8,841.70.
• Taiwan’s Taiex jumped 2%, while India’s Sensex rose 0.7%.
• U.S. markets logged their biggest losses since October on Tuesday.
• Trump had threatened tariffs on eight European countries for opposing U.S. control of Greenland.
• On Wednesday, the S&P 500 climbed 1.2% to 6,875.
• The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 1.2% to 49,077.23.
• The Nasdaq composite also rose 1.2%, to 23,224.82.
• The price of gold fell 0.9% to $4,794.70 per ounce.
• The yield on the 10-year Treasury eased to 4.25% from 4.30% late Tuesday.
• U.S. benchmark crude oil gained 0.3% to $60.79 per barrel.
• Brent crude rose 0.2% to $65.35 per barrel.
• The U.S. dollar rose to 158.54 Japanese yen from 158.27 yen.
• The euro was mostly unchanged at $1.1693.
